overview: **Studying Postgraduate Automobile Engineering France** is a popular choice for students wishing to specialize in vehicle design, automotive systems, electric mobility, powertrain technology and sustainable transportation.
**Edu Hawk worldwide** study abroad guidance can make students aware of these opportunities and requirements involved in pursuing education overseas.

sections.title: 1.** Can international students pursue Automobile Engineering in France?

items: Yes. International students (including Indian students) can apply for eligible automotive engineering masters and specialist programs if they meet the academic, language and application requirements.

sections.title: 2. FAQ What French universities provide post-graduate automotive engineering?

items: For the **Automotive Engineering for Sustainable Mobility master's programme**students may also consider ISAT and Polytech Orléans, in addition to ESTACA and ISAE-Supméca for suitable automotive or mechanical engineering tracks.

sections.title: 3. Do you have postgraduate courses in automobile engineering in English?

items: Yep. The AESM program is a joint program offered by Polytech Orléans and ISAT in English language. Some other programs may be taught in French or a combination of languages, so students should check the language for the intake that they are interested in.

sections.title: 4. What is the fee structure for Automobile Engineering PG in France?

items: Tuition fees depend on the qualification and institution. For the academic year 2026-2027 the national reference fee for a subsidized Master’s degree course is €3,950 per year for non-EU students subject to differentiated fees. The Université d'Orléans has AESM at 5,750 €/year. Students are responsible to check with the institutions concerned.

sections.title: 5. What are the job opportunities after PG in Automobile Engineering in France?

items: Graduate career options include vehicle design, electric vehicle systems, powertrain development, testing, simulation, manufacturing, motorsport and automotive research. The opportunities you will have in your career depend on your experience, your specialization, the languages you speak, and the requirements of the employer.

sections.title: 8. Recognition and Accreditation of Automobile Engineering Degrees in France**

items: When enrolling for a ****Automobile Engineering postgraduate program in France****students should not just look at the program title but also check the qualification awarded by the institution.
The main types of qualifications to know are:
- **Master’s Degree:** A master’s degree recognized at the national level within the French higher education system.
- **Engineering diploma**: obtained from an authorized engineering school. Recognition and status depends on the particular diploma.
- **Postgraduate Specialisation:** A professional or specialist course that does not correspond to a national master’s degree.
The AESM program is listed by Université d’Orléans as a co-accredited Master’s level program with ISAT, registered at level BAC+5.
Before you apply, students should check:
- the official title of the degree and the institution that granted it.
- whether the program leads to a national master’s degree, an engineering diploma or a specialization.
- The institution’s accreditation or recognition status.
- duration and academic credits.
- requirements for recognition of employment or further study in the destination country.

sections.title: 9. Salary and Job Opportunities After Automobile Engineering PG in France**

items: A ****Master’s in Automobile Engineering in France**** opens up the door to job prospects in vehicle development, automotive systems, electric mobility, manufacturing, testing and research.
The employment outcomes are dependent on the specialization, practical experience, language skills, location and labor market conditions.
Possible **jobs after Automobile Engineering PG in France** are:
* Automotive Design Engineer
* Vehicle Dynamics Engineer
* Electric Vehicle Systems Engineer
* Powertrain Engineer
* Automotive Simulation Engineer
* Automotive Electronics or Embedded-Systems Engineer
* Testing and Validation Engineer
* Automotive Manufacturing Engineer
* Motorsport Engineer
* Research and Development Engineer
* Sustainable Mobility Engineer

Potential employers include car manufacturers, suppliers of vehicle components, electric mobility companies, engineering consultancies, testing organizations, motorsport companies and research laboratories.
**Automobile Engineering Salary in France**
There is no one salary for all automobile engineering graduates. Pay varies according to experience, duties, employer, location and technical specialization.

French language skills are useful for local employment, teamwork and communication with manufacturers and suppliers. Graduates who wish to pursue research, either in academia or in industry, may also do a PhD if they meet the relevant entry requirements.

sections.title: 10. Documents Needed for Automobile Engineering PG in France**

items: The checklist is specific to institutions. Documents generally asked for admission in Automobile Engineering in France are:
- Accepted identity document or valid passport.
- Bachelor’s Degree Certificate / Provisional Certificate.
- Academic transcripts and marksheets.
- Resume or CV.
- Motivation letter or statement of purpose.
- Test results in English or French as appropriate.
- Letters of recommendation, if desired.
- Course descriptions or syllabus of prior study where applicable.
- Certificates of internship or employment (if applicable).
- Technical project or research details if asked.
- Certified translations of documents if required.
- Application form completed.
- Receipt of application fee, if any.

With the AESM application form you need to submit a CV, a copy of your passport, a motivation letter, the curriculum of your undergraduate course, your degree certificates, your transcripts, two reference letters and your English-language test results.
The checklist for the academic application is different from the visa and enrollment documents. Upon receiving an admission decision, students must adhere to the official instructions provided.
